subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] How can I specify F1xF1 family as a covariate for an MQM model with a complicated cross design?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] How can I specify F1xF1 family as a covariate for an MQM model with a complicated cross design?
parts:
> I'm stumped as to how to specify family as a cofactor for an MQM model I'm trying to test. I am working with a complex outbred mapping population in which 40 F1 fish (from an intercross between two species) were allowed to freely interbred in a pond, in order to produce F2 hybrids for mapping.

In the QTL formula, you need to refer to the columns in the covariate matrix by their names. It would be best to give them simpler names than they currently have:

colnames(family_cofactor) <- paste("fam", 1:ncol(family_cofactor), sep="")

Then I'd use a bit of code to make the long formula, rather than typing it.

myformula <- "y ~ Q1+Q2+Q3+Q4+Q5+Q6+Q9+Q10+Q11+Q12+Q13+Q1:Q11+Q1:Q13+Q3:Q12+Q4:Q12+Q10:Q11"
myformula <- paste(myformula, "+", paste(colnames(family_cofactor), collapse="+"), sep="+")


output <- fitqtl(miAll.29fam.gp, pheno.col="isotope_pc1", covar=family_cofactor,
qtl=All_Candidate_QTL_for_PC1, get.ests=TRUE, method="hk",
formula=myformula)

karl

> It's easy to specify family as an additive cofactor for single QTL mapping with the function scanone, as follows:
>
> family <- as.character(pull.pheno(miAll.29fam,"family"))
> familymatrix <- model.matrix(~ family)[,-1]
> miAll.29fam.hk <- scanone(miAll.29fam.gp, pheno.col=4:nc, method="hk",addcovar=familymatrix)
>
> This works without a problem.
>
> However, I've tried two approaches for specifying family as a cofactor for MQM modeling, both of which result in problems:

> new_family<-pull.pheno(miAll.29fam.gp,"family")
> family_number <- as.numeric(new_family)
> family_cofactor <- data.frame(family_number=family_number)
> head(family_cofactor)
> # family_number
> # 1 55
> # 2 55
> # 3 55
> # 4 55
> # 5 55
> # 6 55
> # Here, families are named with different integer numbers.
> # There are 28 families larger than a sufficient size cut-off,
> # which is why family numbers go higher than 28.

> out.fq1.4 <- fitqtl(miAll.29fam.gp, pheno.col="isotope_pc1", covar=family_cofactor,
> qtl=All_Candidate_QTL_for_PC1, get.ests=TRUE, method="hk",
> formula=y~Q1+Q2+Q3+Q4+Q5+Q6+Q9+Q10+Q11+Q12+Q13+family_number+
> Q1:Q11 + Q1:Q13 + Q3:Q12 + Q4:Q12 + Q10:Q11)
